requested_behavior: Support user-declared deep-learning/reinforcement-learning packages in the explicitly selected Python environment. Package presence must not silently install anything, change interpreter, or bind a framework/trainer. Distinguish package importability from first-party adapter support.
implementation: Added `m-model env libraries` with repeatable `--library` filters and explicit `--venv` selection; absent `--python` follows the saved project environment if present, while explicit `--python` takes precedence.

Library discovery runs a fixed standard-library metadata query in the selected interpreter. It does not import third-party packages, invoke entry points, install dependencies, switch interpreters, or select a model/training backend.

Reports known package distribution versions and separates `installed` metadata from `adapter_status`: native PyTorch support is identified; torchvision, timm, Lightning, Transformers, Diffusers, JAX/Flax, Gymnasium, Stable-Baselines3, and Ray are package-only; arbitrary distributions are unknown.
Human terminal output and JSON reports explain selection, versions, and the no-auto-install/no-auto-bind boundary. Missing explicitly requested venv paths fail closed rather than falling back.
Added a worker capability, Rust request-feature routing, embedded worker asset, and compatibility-contract entry for `environment.library_inventory`.

Removed the implicit PyTorch requirement from environment lock validation and resolution. `env lock`, `env setup`, and wheelhouse operations now process the user-declared requirements closure; they do not add Torch or select a runtime adapter.

Kept Model-Maven model inspection fail-closed when the selected environment lacks Torch. The non-Torch regression prepares a one-package environment, verifies metadata inventory, and observes `OPERATION_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE` with the PyTorch requirement explained in readiness.

Added explicit `m-model env probe --library <id>` as a separate operation from metadata-only inventory. It imports only allowlisted, user-named ML/RL candidates in the selected interpreter and reports imported/not-installed/import-failed, detected versions, exception type, and sanitized failure reason.

Registered `environment.library_probe` as an informational capability that remains available without Torch. Probe never installs packages, changes interpreters, or binds a backend/Trainer; package-only candidates remain package-only even after a successful import.

Removed the duplicated candidate-to-distribution/import mapping from the probe subprocess source. The parent now passes the pair directly from `_LIBRARIES`, so inventory, allowlisting, import names, and adapter labels share one registry and cannot silently drift apart.

Added opt-in `m-model env probe --check-runtime` as a distinct check level. PyTorch runs fixed CPU tensor arithmetic; torchvision exercises CPU NMS; JAX runs CPU array arithmetic; Gymnasium samples a bounded Box. Each library runs in a fresh subprocess, at most four per command. The report separates import status from runtime_check status (passed/failed/unsupported/not_run), keeps auto_installed/auto_bound false, and unsupported library profiles do not imply a backend.

limitations: Distribution metadata presence does not prove importability, native ABI health, or successful initialization; library inventory deliberately avoids executing third-party code.

Only the existing native PyTorch execution backend is first-party supported. Generic lock/setup can prepare user-declared JAX/Flax/Gymnasium/other dependencies but does not add their Model-Maven model/training loops or bind a Trainer.

Import probing intentionally executes candidate package initialization code in a subprocess with the current user permissions; it is a diagnostic, not a sandbox or a safety guarantee for third-party packages.

Opt-in CPU runtime profiles currently cover PyTorch, torchvision, JAX and Gymnasium only; other allowlisted packages report unsupported. GPU/ROCm/CUDA initialization is not claimed, and explicit package imports/runtime checks execute third-party code with the selected interpreter permissions.

Only the PyTorch 2.15.0 CPU profile has current live-package acceptance evidence. torchvision, JAX and Gymnasium runtime branches are exercised with disposable fixture packages; real installations were absent in the measured interpreter and remain unverified.
